## 2025-02-14 - Fix Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Auto-Report Generator
**Vulnerability:** The HTML technical reports generated by the interpolation pipeline (`backend/app/services/report_service.py`) were vulnerable to XSS. User-controlled or external data, such as job IDs, layer IDs, alert descriptions, trajectories, and statuses, were being formatted into an HTML string using Python f-strings without any sanitization or escaping.
**Learning:** Generating HTML content manually via f-strings bypassing templating engines that handle automatic escaping (like Jinja2) creates a high risk for XSS vulnerabilities, particularly if any interpolated parameters can contain unvalidated dynamic content. Furthermore, when fixing these issues, care must be taken to convert potentially non-string types to strings before passing them to `html.escape()` and string truncations must occur prior to the escape operation to prevent malformed HTML. Also, using the variable name `html` in the function scope shadows the python `html` module and causes referencing errors.
**Prevention:** Avoid generating manual HTML via string interpolation. Utilize established templating libraries (e.g., Jinja2) that escape output context-sensitively by default. If manual HTML generation is strictly necessary, ensure all dynamic values (e.g., `job_id`, `layer_id`, `status`) are explicitly and correctly sanitized using `html.escape(str(value))` before interpolation, paying special attention to truncation orders and preventing module shadowing.
